coverage: Pier & Point covers four sites on San Francisco's central waterfront: Mission Rock, Mission Bay, Pier 70 and Potrero Power Station. A parcel that is not in this data is outside coverage, not "no activity".

record.name: William J. Rutter Center
record.summary: A community center of about 150,000-156,000 sq ft (four to five stories, sources differ) at 1675 Owens St (OpenStreetMap), housing a fitness center, a conference center with an auditorium, a gymnasium, swimming pools, a food court and offices, designed by Legorreta Arquitectos with MBT Architecture; Legorreta's project page lists the year 2005.

notes.accuracy_caveat: REAL -- surveyed OpenStreetMap building footprint, not a hand trace or plan estimate; the west edge is idealized to a straight line (2 points instead of the OSM trace's 3, dropping a sub-meter digitizing jog), not a surveyed change. This is the opposite situation from Mission Bay's condo-mapped residential towers (Avalon, Radiance, etc.): here, ONE large Assessor land parcel spans SEVERAL UCSF buildings (confirmed against DataSF's Assessor parcel data and tax roll -- e.g. block/lot 8711507 (675 Mission Bay Blvd in DataSF's parcel data) alone is about 12.2 acres, far larger than any single building on it), so using the parcel boundary per building would make multiple records overlap and double-count the same ground. The real building footprint is the only non-overlapping, honest shape for this record.
notes.digitized_from: OpenStreetMap (way 84812339: name 'UCSF Community Center', official name 'William J. Rutter Center', address 1675 Owens St). Its own small mid-edge digitizing jog on the west wall was straightened into a clean 4-corner quadrilateral on 2026-09-22. How this shape was traced, including earlier versions, is logged in its data file in the public data repository (https://github.com/pierandpoint/record).

costs.what: Total project budget the UC Regents approved in March 2000 for the Mission Bay Campus Community Center Building (21B), confirmed as this building by matching architects and program, per the May 2000 Regents design-approval item that recounts the budget action

milestones.text: UC Regents item for the Committee on Grounds and Buildings (May 2000) recommends certifying an EIR addendum and approving the design of the Mission Bay Campus Community Center Building (21B) -- this building, confirmed by matching architects (MBT Architecture as executive architect with Legorreta Arquitectos as design subconsultant) and program (fitness/recreation center, conference center, food service, retail); the item recounts that the Regents approved a $58,000,000 total project cost in March 2000 and states construction 'will begin in 2001 and be completed in 2002'. The item is the recommendation; the committee's action itself is not shown

This building's photo (from a Sept. 2008 Regents presentation) has no independently confirmed capture date; it predates or coincides with that presentation, which is well after the building's own completion date, so it is shown as a current ('now') view, being the only photograph found, rather than a 'completed' view. No site plan or rendering specific to this building was found in a public-record source.

Corrected 2026-09-29: the names 'Bakar Fitness & Recreation Center' and 'Mission Bay Conference Center', the description 'Mexican-modernist', and 'opened as part of Mission Bay's first development phase' are in none of the cited pages (Legorreta, Forell, OpenStreetMap) and were removed; the building's names in sources are 'William J. Rutter Center' (OpenStreetMap's official name, Forell) and 'UCSF Community Center' (OpenStreetMap's name, Legorreta). The 2008 Regents photo's capture date is not given (the presentation is dated September 2008), so the year it was taken was removed; showing it as a current ('now') view is also doubtful for a photo of that age.

record.notes: ~150,000-156,600 sq ft (sources vary), four to five stories; houses a fitness center, conference center with an auditorium, gymnasium, swimming pools, food court and offices (Legorreta; Forell). The names 'Bakar Fitness & Recreation Center' and 'Mission Bay Conference Center' are not in any cited source. Architect Legorreta Arquitectos (Ricardo and Victor Legorreta) with MBT Architecture as associate/executive architect. Legorreta's project page lists the year 2005 (opening month not confirmed by a primary source). Per UCSF's own Dec 2024-updated campus map, this is Block 21B; the adjoining Community Center Garage to its west is the separate Block 21A (mapped as its own record).
